title: Review of Fire Safety Standards for HDB Blocks and Installation of Home Fire Alarm Devices for all HDB Public Rental Flats
what_it_is: Review of Fire Safety Standards for HDB Blocks and Installation of Home Fire Alarm Devices for all HDB Public Rental Flats

sections.label: HFAD scheme in rental flats
sections.summary: The HFAD Assistance Scheme for HDB public rental flats was completed in June 2021 with a 75% take-up rate, and remaining flats will be installed progressively at lease end.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Home Fire Alarm Device (HFAD) Assistance Scheme, which provided for free installation of HFADs for all HDB public rental flats on a non-mandatory basis, was completed in June 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The take-up rate as of the completion of the initiative was 75%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: HDB will progressively install HFADs in the remaining 25% of public rental flats when their tenants' leases end.

sections.label: Fire extinguisher trial at lift lobbies
sections.summary: SCDF is trialling with HDB, Town Councils and Temasek Foundation to place and maintain one fire extinguisher at a lift lobby of every two HDB blocks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: SCDF is embarking on a trial with HDB, Town Councils and Temasek Foundation to place and maintain one fire extinguisher at a lift lobby of every two HDB blocks for use by residents during fire emergencies.

sections.label: Non-fire-rated doors under HIP
sections.summary: Under the prevailing Fire Code, many households with existing fire-rated doors are offered non-fire-rated doors as replacements under the Home Improvement Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Based on the prevailing Fire Code, a significant number of households having existing fire-rated doors are being offered non-fire-rated doors as replacement under the Home Improvement Programme (HIP).

sections.label: Fire-rated doors, hoarding engagement question
sections.summary: Residents may opt for fire-rated doors at their own expense if not required by the Fire Code, and the passage asks whether more trained officers and paid workers should lead hoarder engagement and clearance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Residents may opt to install fire-rated doors even where this is not required under the Fire Code, but this would be at their own expense, as there is a cost difference between fire-rated and non-fire-rated doors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: If the Fire Code does not require fire-rated doors, this additional cost will not be covered under the HIP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I know that there is currently a multi-agency approach to hoarding cases and it often involves engaging volunteers to persuade the hoarders and to help clear the items.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am very grateful for the big-hearted work of these volunteers, but given that there may be urgent public health and safety issues at stake, does the Senior Minister of State agree that there is a need to deploy more trained and experienced officers to lead the engagement of the hoarders and for paid workers to help with the clearance so that it can be done more expeditiously?

sections.label: Hoarding not an illness
sections.summary: Mental health colleagues have learnt that hoarding itself is not an illness or a condition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For instance, what we have learnt from our mental health colleagues is that hoarding itself is not an illness or a condition.

sections.label: SCDF on cluttered homes fire risk
sections.summary: SCDF does not generally assess cluttered homes as a key fire risk, and is working with the inter-agency HMCG to look into the issue.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As I shared earlier, SCDF does not assess cluttered homes, in general, to be a key fire risk.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, at the end of the day, we have to look at the different cases.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: However, that said, we understand the Member's and the public's concern; and we are working closely with the inter-agency HMCG to look into the issue.
